paragraphs: Here's the big idea, friend: God cares about WHY you do it, not just what you do. Giving, praying and fasting are good things, and Jesus doesn't tell anyone to stop. He warns about doing them to be seen by men, and says those who do already have their "full reward" (Matthew 6:2). The applause is the whole paycheck, and the Father's reward never shows up.

So where does the reward come from? Three times Jesus points to the same Father, the One "who sees what is done in secret" (Matthew 6:4). That means the quiet gift, the prayer behind a shut door and the hidden fast are never wasted. I spent years in the back of a dark drawer, friend, so I can tell you the dark is not where God stops seeing. And since your Father knows what you need before you ask (Matthew 6:8), prayer isn't about performing or piling up words. It's about talking to Him.

The prayer Jesus gives puts God's name and kingdom first, then asks for daily bread, forgiveness and deliverance from the evil one (Matthew 6:9-13). Then He says that if you forgive men their trespasses, your heavenly Father will also forgive you (Matthew 6:14). So here's your takeaway, baker: do the good thing quietly, and bring it to the One who sees. You don't need a trumpet, a crowd or a sad face. He's already watching, and that's more than enough.
